messages:
maria: Quick sync — I ran a head-to-head between the replay harness and our synthetic long-context generator for a prefill-heavy workload and the numbers disagree by ~18% on mean latency.
bench-bot: (auto) replay-run-1912345678: 1h run complete. avg p50=210ms p95=890ms p99=1.4s tokens/sec=3200
anya: Can you paste the exact config? seq dist / batch / KV warm settings?
jules: Config: `seq_dist: long_prefill`, `batching: adaptive_v2`, `kv_policy: warm_on_prefill`, `kernels: auto` — default replay harness params.
pranav: The synth generator used `seqlen=4096/50%` + `1024/30%` + `256/20%` and artificially linear inter-arrival, batching=simulated-continuous (no client-side jitter)
maria: Replay was a user session replay (real inter-arrival jitter + real prefix reuse). I expected synth to be a bit cleaner; wasn't expecting synth to be faster.
jules: Interesting — synth not priming KV cache like replay does? That usually helps prefill-heavy workloads.
kevin: We saw a kernel selection fallback in recent canary when effective seq_len > 2048 for certain attention patterns; that slowed per-token. Could explain synth/replay diff if synth has many mid-range sequences.
anya: Can we get profiler breakdown? prefill vs decode token time, kernel switch overhead, memcpy, and KV lookup time.
bench-bot: (auto) profile-summary-1912345699: prefill=64% decode=28% memcpy+overhead=8% (small sample)
jules: That profile looks like prefill-dominant as expected. But memcpy+overhead jumps when we hit fallback kernel.
maria: I attached a tiny log snippet from the kernel selector.
```
[2026-03-15T10:12:08Z] seq_len=3072 op=select_kernel -> chosen=fused_attention_fp16_v2
[2026-03-15T10:12:08Z] seq_len=3072 op=fallback -> chosen=generic_attention
[2026-03-15T10:12:08Z] note=memcpy_peak 12MB latency_penalty +18%
```
pranav: That fallback pattern would definitely widen the gap. Replay might have kept more small prefills to stay in fused path while synth produced many medium clips.
kevin: Actionable: generate a synthetic run that mimics replay's prefix reuse distribution (i.e., % of exact prefix hits, reuse distance histogram). Then compare.
anya: Also propose an apples-vs-head approach: run both harnesses with identical sequence distribution and identical scheduling jitter so kernel decisions only differ because of runtime nondeterminism.
sam: Suggest measuring two extra metrics: kernel-change-count per minute, and KV-hit-rate-on-prefill. Those should surface the root cause.
jules: I can add kernel-change-count to the runtime counters. Meanwhile I ran a short A/B with synth altered to include prefix reuse: p50 now 216ms p95 910ms — gap narrows to 6%.
maria: Nice. Could be that original synth underrepresented reuse. Any regression from the latest fused-kernel micro-optimizations that could bite on prefill-heavy streams?
kevin: There was a recent micropatch that added an extra memcpy when building KV shards for large prefills; it was gated but the selector now enables it for certain block sizes. I'll bisect.
pranav: For the head-to-head benchmark, propose this protocol:
- canonical seqlen histogram from live traffic
- replay harness playback of N sessions (make noise model explicit)
- synthetic generator seeded from same histogram and same inter-arrival jitter
- pin model version + kernel flags
- record metrics: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, kernel-change-count, kv-hit-rate, memcpy_bytes, fallback-events
- run 5x and report median
anya: + include a short standalone run with `kv_preload=true` to measure ideal primed baseline.
sam: I'll add dashboards for kernel-change-count and fallback-events. ETA end of day.
jules: After bisect, I found the extra memcpy in commit `c4f9b2` — reverting it on canary removed the memcpy spike and synth/replay numbers aligned within 2% on our test sample.
maria: Great find. Let's roll that revert to staging and re-run full 1h head-to-head.
kevin: Will schedule. Also filing a follow-up perf-issue with the micropatch details.
bench-bot: (auto) run-scheduled 1912345780: full 1h head-to-head queued
maria: Thanks all — this is a good reminder that synthetic generators need to capture prefix-reuse and that small memcpy policy changes can disproportionately affect prefill workloads. :white_check_mark:
